readme.html:
OpenOSINT is an open-source OSINT agent for investigators and security researchers: 21 public-source tools behind a natural-language interface, with an MCP server.

Run it yourself: uvx openosint web (one command, no keys)
No terminal? Run a quick check in the browser, first check free

Docs · Claude Code plugin · MCP server

Quickstart

Needs uv. No API keys for these commands.

# Local web app with chat, graph and globe
uvx openosint web

# Or one direct check, no AI involved
uvx openosint exposure example.com

Grade: B  Score: 88/100
Checks: email OK, registration OK (passive)
        tls OK, http_headers OK (these touch the target)
  [LOW] DMARC has no aggregate report address (dmarc_no_rua)
  [LOW] Strict-Transport-Security header missing (hsts_missing)

Real output, trimmed and re-wrapped. More commands: CLI reference · install guide.

Not a developer?

The same engine powers the OpenOSINT Investigator Board, a hosted case board for investigators: company lookups with sources, confirmed connections and a signed PDF report. See a sample case rebuilt from public records: Azerbaijani Laundromat. For a one-off check on a company, website or email sender, use Quick check in the browser; the first check is free, no account needed.

What you can do

Moved to Quickstart above and the CLI reference.

Tools

What it can look up. Per-tool docs: openosint.tech/tools. Only passive tools are on by default.

Tool What it finds Key needed
search_dns DNS records, SPF, DMARC No
search_rdap Registrar, dates, name servers (RDAP) No
search_whois WHOIS registration data No
search_ip Hostname, ASN, city for an IP Optional
search_ip2location Geolocation, ISP, proxy/VPN/Tor flags (sponsored) Yes
search_gdelt_geo Geolocated news mentions (GDELT) No
generate_dorks Search-dork URLs for a target No
search_paste Paste-site mentions No
search_github Repos, code and users Optional
search_breach Breaches for an email (HaveIBeenPwned) Yes
search_shodan Open ports and banners Yes
search_censys Hosts and certificates Yes
search_virustotal URL, domain and IP reputation Yes
search_abuseipdb IP abuse reports Yes
search_dorks_live Live dork results via Bright Data SERP API¹ Yes
search_footprint Web footprint via Bright Data SERP API¹ Yes
scrape_url Page content via Bright Data Web Unlocker¹ (touches target) Yes
search_username Username across platforms (sherlock; noisy) No
search_email Accounts tied to an email (holehe; noisy) No
search_domain Subdomains (sublist3r; noisy) No
search_phone Carrier and country (phoneinfoga; unverified) No

Sherlock, holehe, sublist3r and phoneinfoga run as local binaries you install yourself. Setting up the Bright Data tools: Using OpenOSINT with Bright Data.

Why OpenOSINT

Tools run as real Python code and every finding cites the call that produced it. Compared with SpiderFoot, OpenOSINT has far fewer modules and is built to be driven by an agent. See the comparison.

Passive by default

Agents and MCP clients are only offered tools that query third-party sources or compute locally. Anything that touches the target or sends many requests from your IP is off until you opt in (--allow-active) and is not listed in an MCP client's tools/list. Passive is not private: every service you query sees the query. Details: Safety.

Use it from Claude Code or any MCP client

/plugin marketplace add OpenOSINT/OpenOSINT
/plugin install openosint@openosint
/openosint:osint example.com

claude mcp add openosint -- uvx --from openosint openosint-mcp
# Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor and other Agent Skills clients
npx skills add OpenOSINT/OpenOSINT

Other clients: MCP docs · Agent Skill.
